item.title: Project Hail Mary, 2026 - ★★★★½
item.description:
I had very high expectations for this film, being a fan of the book and the creators (Ryan, Lord & Miller, Greig Fraser) - and this absolutely delivered.

I would wholeheartedly recommend watching this in theaters, because the visuals are a treat, and the shared joy is palpable.

It's 4.5* only because it seemed that the movie dragged in a few spots, and some of the key plot points seemed to resolve very quickly. However, the film is amazing despite any of those concerns.

AMAZE. AMAZE. AMAZE!
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning, 2025 - ★★★★
item.description:
This is a fitting send-off for likely the greatest action-movie franchise of all time. Although the movie takes too long to get going, with nearly 1/3rd of the movie being exposition, each of the set pieces are insane and ratchet up the tension well beyond where you think they'd peak.

The final climax (and knowing that Tom was actually doing these stunts) is an insane and stunning amount of spectacle. The movie has too many convieniences, but this is par for the course for MI (much like the mention of family, in a different franchise)

This isn't my favourite mission team, but Benji, Grace and Ethan hold it together. I'd have loved to see folks like Brandt (Jeremy Renner) or Jane return, but I did welcome some of the new faces.

While this movie doesn't come close to the incredible trio of Ghost Protocol, Rogue Nation and Fallout, it is still a worthy addition to the franchise.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: The Wild Robot, 2024 - ★★★★★
item.description:
A beautiful, heartfelt and joyous story that is lovingly animated and voiced.

I did not expect this movie to hit me as hard as it did, but while my kids enjoyed the story and the action, I was floored by how it was a perfect microcosm of being a parent.

This is easily one of my top 3 movies of the year. One of the best non-franchise animated movies in recent times, along with "Mitchells vs. the Machines".
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Transformers One, 2024 - ★★★★★
item.description:
As a child who grew up with the original Transformers movie, and enjoyed the spectacle (and decay) of the live action Bay Transformers, I was skeptical of this movie. The trailers did not do the movie justice either.

Watching my kid's face light up throughout the film brought me back to my own childhood wonder. Despite having no prior connection to the franchise, he was completely captivated by the characters – and surprisingly, so was I. This movie reignited my love for Transformers and created a new fan in my son.

Sure, the plot occasionally takes convenient turns, and the middle act slows for exposition. But the finale, while predictable, still manages to surprise and delight.

Highly recommended, especially for jaded fans like myself or for parents who want to expose their kids (and wallets) to this beloved franchise.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, 2023 - ★★★★
item.description:
A heartfelt and fitting bookend to a band of characters who had no business being this beloved.

Almost every character gets a convincing arc despite this being wholly Rocket's movie.

Guardians movies are known for their soundtrack and although the first one will be near and dear to my heart, Vol. 3 might be my actual favourite one of them all.

The ending song choice and montage is pitch perfect and I'm so glad they wrapped the movie up as they did.

I can't wait to see what James Gunn does with Superman after this.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse, 2023 - ★★★★★
item.description:
It's unfathomable to me how a movie can top one of the greatest Spiderman, scratch that, one of the best superhero movies of all time.

The original changed the animated movie style after it came out. It's incredible to me how this movie is an even better looking movie than that. Characters move, evoke, emote and evolve in gorgeous ways.

The story is a perfect Spiderman story and the stakes are heavy.

I am so glad I got to see this in theaters and I cannot wait to come back to see it.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: John Wick: Chapter 4, 2023 - ★★★★★
item.description:
Exactly what this movie needed to be and then some. It's probably one of the best action films from probably the best action film franchise.

It's gorgeously shot, stylishly produced and the violence is a character and a language in itself. The new characters are all really well done and they fit right into the movie.

Keanu Reeves was already a legend and having now been in two incredible franchises - doing this at 58 years of age, is just... breathtaking.

The ending is perfect and it's fitting for the character. Easily the best movie of the year so far.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once, 2022 - ★★★★★
item.description:
What's to say about this movie that hasn't been said already.

It's the weirdest and most wonderful movie I saw last year.

An absolute showcase of some legends that have been under appreciated and the best multiverse movie to come in a year which literally had a movie called "Multiverse of Madness"
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: The Super Mario Bros. Movie, 2023 - ★★★★
item.description:
Colorful, cheery and chock full of Easter eggs for both young fans and fans that grew up with the games. The voice acting is surprisingly good considering the backlash. Jack Black's Bowser and Toad are excellent in particular.

This is a perfect family movie and it's a wonder why it took so long to make a great Mario Bros movie.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Bullet Train, 2022 - ★★★★★
item.description:
This is my favourite movie of 2022. A fantastic cast anchored by Brad Pitt, who almost never misses a beat. The interwoven story with the unexpected but awesome pairing of Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Brian Tyree Henry is then underlined with the stylized production and the music.

Someone said it feels like a live-action anime and I agree with it. Highly recommended!
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Uncharted, 2022 - ★★½
item.description:
Inoffensive, but also unsubstantial. Silly popcorn entertainment. Good for some background viewing - nothing really substantial, except the charisma of Tom Holland playing a significantly younger Nathan Drake.

It was great to see Nolan North in a small cameo appearance.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, 2022 - ★★★½
item.letterboxd:filmTitle: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
item.description:
overall, the leads are at the top of their game. Sam Raimi does a very stylized version of the horror / comedy style he did in Evil Dead. this is basically the closest we get to MCU horror.

the movie itself while visually entertaining and certainly had its moments, ultimately, ends up being a filler movie.

Despite telling a smaller story, the primary purpose of the movie is to setup the next phase for MCU and Dr. Strange himself. It does so by mentioning a word that is sure to trigger a specific event with fans of the comics.

The movie does have many loose threads still open, so the overall placement of the movie is going to depend on what comes next. I think the biggest detractor of the movie is that it feels like episode 7-9 of WandaVision.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: CODA, 2021 - ★★★★★
item.description:
I thought this was going to be a paint by numbers kind of movie, but the utterly charming and heartwarming performances elevated this movie immensely.

Each family member has a dynamic between them and that is sufficiently explored within the movie. I'm also happy that the "romance" elements in the movie were not highlighted as expected, so that the main character's passion and dreams could shine more.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: The French Dispatch of the Liberty, Kansas Evening Sun, 2021 - ★★★★
item.letterboxd:filmTitle: The French Dispatch of the Liberty, Kansas Evening Sun
item.description:
While visually beautiful as most Wes Anderson's movies are, the final product is only slightly affected by it feeling like a bunch of shorts.

Highly entertaining and I love how Wes Anderson does black comedy. Especially in the short featuring Timothee Chalamet.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: The Batman, 2022 - ★★★★½
item.description:
Fantastic cast, a vibe and tone fitting Gotham coupled with deliberate pacing makes this my 2nd all time favourite Batman movie.

(Heath Ledger's incredible performance still keeps Dark Knight as #1 for now)
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home, 2021 - ★★★★★
item.description:
A love letter to fans of the Spiderman movies. Once the bridge scene happens, each scene is nearly pitch perfect. All the returns (though heavily rumored and spoiled) were still incredible to witness and it felt like all the characters got a fair shake despite a stuffed cast.

Willem Dafoe absolutely steals the scene in a series of amazing performances. This is the strongest outing from Tom Holland's version of the character and they finally brought the "truest" form of the character through.

The only thing missing from this movie was Stan Lee.

What an incredible movie, a fascinating ride and I cannot wait to see what's in store next.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Dune, 2021 - ★★★★★
item.description:
Denis Villeneuve had previously made one of my favourite films of all time (Arrival), so the hype going into this was massive. Add to that a star-studded cast and some very compelling trailers. As a fan of the book, I wasn't sure the movie could deliver, but I genuinely hoped it would.

Deliver it did! One of my most enjoyable theater-movies, especially in the IMAX presentation which sinks you into this tangible, and believable world of the (movie) Dune.

I cannot wait for Part 2!
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Better Luck Tomorrow, 2002 - ★★★
item.description:
Watched this as a precursor to Tokyo Drift. I really like Justin Lin as an action director, this felt like an early passion project.

It's a decent if unfocused coming of age movie. It has a lot of style and a few hints at Justin's later flairs and camera angles. Although the movie resolves itself I can't help but feel that there was something missing.

Han is the coolest and that hasn't changed.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Luca, 2021 - ★★★½ (contains spoilers)
item.description:
This review may contain spoilers.

This is a gorgeously rendered movie. The landscapes are breathtaking and every leaf and dew drop are beautiful. It reminded me of our trip to the Amalfi Coast.

However looks aside, this is an odd entry in the Pixar movies lineup. It's cheery, fairly low stakes and warm but it lacks the depth and rewatchability of the best Pixar movies. I'd describe it as "breezy".

Why do the characters talk in English but with Italian accents? Why are the fish people helping people fish? Does the rest of the world just shrug at the fish person going to school now?

All that and other deeper questions aside, the movie is lovely to see and a chill watch.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: The Mitchells vs. the Machines, 2021 - ★★★★★
item.description:
Heartwarming and gorgeously animated to look like it fits with the 2009-2010 era of social media. Despite a hilariously over-the-top plot as well some ridiculous stunts, the warmth of the characters and the love of the family keeps this from spinning off course.

What a wonderful surprise, but also, not a surprise considering this is a team that gave us Into the Spiderverse.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Khan

item.title: Hungama, 2003 - ★★★★
item.description:
Paresh Rawal and a cast of comedy veterans put together a hilarious comedy of errors. It's a bit slow to start, but the ending 1/3rd of the movie is top notch comedy.

Physical comedy becomes apparent as soon as Rajpal Yadav enters the fray, but the writing especially the pun-heavy dialogues don't come off as ham-fisted, which is an accomplishment too.

Harmless fun and a good example of how to do comedy without making it unnecessarily raunchy, or awfully pun-heavy as some of the movies that followed this did.
